text: Good afternoon. This is April Chandler calling to order the Legislative Audit and Policy Committee meeting for May 30th, 2024. We will begin with public comment. Sign up to make in-person public comments occurred prior to the start of the committee meeting.

The meeting will be audio recorded and posted in board docs. Today we have six speakers signed up for public comment. We will allow two minutes. The first speaker is Patricia Caldwell-Wilson, followed by David Milam.
Okay. All righty. Members of the committee, there has been a lot of discussion about collective bargaining.

As a retired Loudoun educator, I know today needs to be about decision-making. We've been in this process to gain collective bargaining for nearly three years. Tactics such as denying membership access to LEA in schools has been detrimental.

having a seat at the table is important to educators. The teachers' work environment is their students' learning environment. The decisions you adopt and send forward today will speak volumes to your educators. Are you willing to make the revisions to the LEA prior to prioritized resolution?

Are you willing to vote each concern up or down? Are we here to support teachers, or are we here to make decisions that will continue the loss of educators, like myself, who left Loudoun after only 14 years because of poor policies and too many years of no pay raises. After teaching in another unionized state before relocating to Virginia 40 years ago, I did not teach my first 19 years in Virginia because there was no union. I'm here today because these meetings are held when teachers are working. They'd love to speak but aren't given the

opportunity. The resolution is in your hands. What is adopted and moved forward today will either show your support for educators or continue the climate of union busting we are experiencing in Loudoun County Public Schools. Thank you. The next speaker is David Milam followed by Corey Brunet.

I'm sorry I'm not wearing red today. All my kids went to the University of Michigan so I wear blue and in Michigan, when my wife Bonnie was a teacher there, they did have a union, the Detroit Public Schools, and she was able to participate in collective bargaining for salary and benefits with others.

I'm a pastor. I preached last Sunday on Leviticus 19, which is famous for love your neighbor as yourself, but it starts with reprove your neighbor when you have a difference, and the reproof is so that you don't have a grudge or become a vengeful.
So we're supposed to talk, in other words, to one another, not kind of talk past each other, have barriers and buffers between us. Collective bargaining allows for people to talk to one another.

It allows for teachers to talk to one another. The passage ends with love your neighbor as yourself. I heard Dr. Spence speak to the equity students a couple of Saturdays ago. He said, we are about loving each other, seeing each other, hearing each other, knowing each other.

I think that very kind of principle that Dr. Spence articulated is the principle that this body of school board members ought to have and embody that sense of letting teachers and staff bargain collectively have their ability to talk to the school board about things that make them great employees and part of this wonderful school system. Thank you very much. Thank you. The next speaker is Corey Brunet followed by Patty

Nelson. I had my eyes dilated not long ago so I don't have anything to read but I did want to take the time to tell you we've already talked about this that this is an agreement between the employees and the school board the employees and the school board the employees and the school

board today is a prime example how many staff members are here versus how many educators are here right now. They couldn't come. I got professional leave. I assume the other, the few that are here also did. They can talk to you whenever they want. We cannot. We need collective bargaining. Thank you. Thank you. The next speaker is Patty Nelson, followed by Andrea Weiskopf.

Hi, I'm Patty Nelson, a longtime resident of Loudoun County. I've been here 32 years. My kids grew up going to Loudoun County schools, and I want to thank you for that. I also want to bring up that regarding collective bargaining for public employees, we are way behind. 47 states had collective bargaining for public employees before Virginia. This is just, it took, I wore out three joints overturning that ban on collective bargaining. And these teachers have waited for

33 months to get a resolution through. The waiting, it's too much waiting. We have waited a long time. I'm the Secretary-Treasurer of SEIU Virginia 512, which is Loudoun County, Fairfax County, Prince William, the City of Richmond, and home care workers around the state. We have been struggling with this in every part of the state. Nobody knows how to do this because it's all brand new for us and the only way to get a fair ordinance for these teachers is to make sure you have teacher voices at the table, that you have LEA voices at the table. When we did the ordinance

in Loudoun County for general services employees, which we won our vote on March 6th, we had union at the table with the board members and we struggled it out and it's the only way to get a fair playing field. So, enough with the union busting in Loudoun County. Thank you. Thank you. The next
speaker is Andrea Weiskopf, followed by Sandy Sullivan.

I took personal leave to be here. For Eisler Dare, LCPS is a job. For Spence, LCPS is a job. He'll probably stick around until his youngest graduates. For Smith, LCPS is a job. He's looking elsewhere. But for most educators, LCPS is more than a job. It is our community. It is our life. For me, LCPS is the children who
trick-or-treat at my door. For me, LCPS is seeing my neighbor's child run on Claiborne with the Stonebridge cross-country team. For me, LCPS is a colleague turned friend.
For me, LCPS is telling the cashier at Giant that he's going to rock his AP exams. For me, LCPS is holding a child who disclosed abuse. For me, LCPS is teaching with a former student.
That is my why. What is Eisler Dare's why? We are LCPS. We belong on that side of the stanchion. Thank you. Black Lives Matter. Thank you.
Our last speaker is Sandy Sullivan. Two years, eight and a half months. 33 months, 1,008 days ago.

Let's really move forward with collective bargaining today. This process for Loudoun educators began two years, eight and a half months ago. 33 months ago, 1,008 days ago. The way to honor the work of your educators today is to make the revisions to the resolution that LEA prioritized.

Today is about decision-making and not just discussion. What we expect to come out of this meeting is revisions to the document, and that moves forward to the full school board. The eight items on our letter to the previous school board, that was a compromise. There were more than 30 egregious items in the resolution that was drafted by Eisler-Dayer, an anti-worker law firm.

With that said, we cannot move forward without addressing an additional item. Our council told us that we must address this item, non-member representation. We're about to do major work on this document, and this is a union and employee issue and not a leadership and staff issue that we need to address.

You do not get to say how the union spends our dues dollars. The Janus decision in 2018 made it so that workers did not have to join the union and made it so workers would not be compelled to pay dues.
The union cannot, the union should not be compelled to represent non-members in grievances. Thank you. All right, we're going to move on to item 3.1, approval of the March 21st, 2024 draft minutes.
Could I please have a motion to approve the meeting minutes? So moved. Thank you, Ms. Donahue, and may I please have a second? Second. Motion was made by Ms. Donahue and seconded by Ms. Chernoff.

All those in favor, please raise your hand and say aye. Aye. The motion passes unanimously with all committee members present for the vote. We will now move on to item 4.1, VSBA positions. Dr. Smith will present.

Dr. Smith, the floor is yours. Thank you, Chair Chandler, board members. At the March meeting of the LAMP committee meeting, four proposals were presented by board members for consideration as statewide legislative positions for the Virginia School Boards Association. One proposal on literacy audits was presented by Ms. Mansfield.

One proposal on firearm safe storage was presented by Ms. Donahue. One proposal on teacher training was presented by Ms. Chernoff. And one proposal on alternate assessment was presented also by Ms. Chernoff. Each of these proposals are presented in board docs today.

Since our March meeting, House Bill 1076 was passed by the General Assembly and signed by the Governor. This bill requires the Board of Education to permit school boards to administer during the 2024 to 2026 school years, assessments as alternatives to our through year growth assessments, also known as the Virginia growth assessments, established by the board.

And this provided that any such alternative assessment is aligned with the standards of learning. And this bill achieves the intent of Ms. Chernoff's alternate assessment proposal. So staff would recommend that you consider these proposals for action today and send them to the full school board.

They are due to the Virginia School Boards Association for their consideration by June 17th, 2024. And so due to the timing, we ask that you maybe consider that in terms of your actions today, but we're happy to answer any questions regarding these proposals or the process you may have.

- Thank you, Dr. Smith. Are there any questions or comments from the committee? - Yes, Mr. Smith. - Thank you, Dr. Smith, for the overview. I had put that proposal in place about the bill in terms of the MAP assessment versus the growth assessment as a way to kind of look at evaluating the true value of doing both.

And I wanted to keep that in there at first because I wasn't sure if the bill was going to be signed. We have more information now, and with that guidance from VDOE, we will be able to move forward with those decisions. So I will be, I would like to, I will be making a motion to get rid of that, as well as I agree with Dr. Smith that we should put this on consent so that we meet the deadline and that our positions can be considered.

So there's no other discussion. I can thank the motion. Is there any other discussion? No, thank you. All right. Seeing no further discussion, would you please make your motion? I move to amend the VSBA LCPS proposals by removing the proposal submitted on state testing and then also moving that this goes to consent.

Second. Thank you. The motion was made by Ms. Chernoff and seconded by Ms. Donahue. All those in favor, please raise your hand and say aye. Aye. Aye. The motion passes unanimously with all committee members present. Thank you.

Mr. Woods, the floor is yours. Thank you. Good afternoon, Chair Chandler, members of the committee. Today, I'm sharing with you OAG's Fiscal Year 2025 Audit Universe.

The audit universe consists of potential audit activities the OAG will perform during the fiscal year 2025. In the universe are carryover audits. These are audits approved for the FY24 audit plan carried over to the FY25 audit plan.
These items will also need to be approved or re-approved to be included into the FY25 audit plan. Below are the fiscal year 2025 audit universe.

In total, there are seven audits to choose from. This pool of audits represents new audit topics for the committee. The committee will have the opportunity to approve of at our next L.A. and P. Committee meeting. Of these seven items, I am recommending that you select three to four audit topics for approval at our next meeting.

The universe was developed with input from stakeholders of different areas within the LCPS environment, which included, but not limited to, board members, members of the cabinet, senior staff, and principals. Thank you, members of the committee, and I welcome any questions you may have.

Thank you, Mr. Woods. Are there any questions or comments from the committee? Ms. Chernoff? Thank you, Mr. Woods. It was great meeting with you and kind of unpacking some of this in more detail. I know next time we're going to vote, and since there's many listed here and we're being asked to consider up to possibly three, maybe four, it seems like three might be more reasonable given the timelines from this year, I just want to put in a personal plug since I have my colleagues here and I can speak to you at this time.

I really would like to look at the school board and staff communication. I think we're also going to be talking about staff aides. I think as a new board, we are establishing a lot of those routines and learning a lot. And I do think that maybe having an audit to look at how that flow of communication, how the data is transferred and how we can receive all of that, I know I would personally find beneficial.

So I'm going to put a plug for that one. And also I'm going to put a plug for transportation. I don't think this will come as any surprise to anyone in terms of how I've been talking a lot about start times and buses and things like that. So I think this will fit in nicely with that work that we're also doing to help give more clarity and fine-tune solutions for our transportation department.

So I'm pretty open to a dialogue about it, but I just wanted to make sure that I went on record with what I would prioritize myself. Thank you, Ms. Chernoff. Any further discussion? No? Oh, well, thank you. On that note, I'll just say I also feel very drawn to the transportation audit.

I'm also very curious about the Jefferson contracts and would like to learn more, but it seems to me that that would be a great way to make sure that we're using our policies efficiently. So with that, thank you so much. And we will move on to item 5.2, policy 2610, Loudoun County School Board aides.

Dr. Smith will present. Dr. Smith, the floor is yours. All right. Thank you, Chair Chandler. Policy 2610, Loudoun County School Board aides. As a part of the FY24 Loudoun County School Board approved budget, an allocation for board aides was provided to each board member.

As board aides have been hired, there's been a need to update and revise policy 2610 to align with LCPS current practices and responsibilities. The red line policy and board docs include several additions and clarifications. You'll notice that we've referenced several other school board policies throughout the document and policies such as policy 1030, policy 1035, and policy 7566. The most substantial update to this policy is in section B, job duties. As we've expanded on the job duties of the board aid, specifically regarding representation in official capacity and communication in meetings.

Additional updates have been made to this section regarding confidentiality to ensure that there is clarity about what can and cannot be shared. This policy revision is presented as an information item today and we're happy to answer any questions you may have. - Thank you, Dr. Smith. I have to say is I'm certainly not the only person at this point who has served as a board aide and a school board member, but this policy is near and dear to my heart.

I think it's important. I know having had that experience myself, I felt a great sense of responsibility to set aside my own activism in terms of what happened at the school board level and to represent the person that I was serving in that capacity at the time.

And I think it solidified my own desire to run for school board, but while I was a staff aide, it was very important to me to put my school board members' needs first. So I'm very excited to have this conversation with my colleagues on this committee and with the full school board.
Are there any other comments or questions? Yes. Ms. Donahue, please. Thank you, Chair Chandler. Thank you, Dr. Smith, for your presentation, for presenting this policy revision.

I did have a few questions. So my first question is with regard to under what circumstances or what the process would be if circumstances arise that would make it appropriate for an aide to be dismissed.
In the current draft, it appears that that is left to the discretion of the member to whom the aide is serving. And I wanted to confirm if my read of that is correct.

That is correct, and that's how it reads, that it's at the discretion of the board member they are serving. There is language in here as well that the board aid also represents the board member in terms of that. And so if there's concerns from other board members around a particular aid, then they would need to address that with their board member.

And so it does address that as well in terms of the expectations around policy 1030, code of conduct, policy 1035 around school board protocols, violations, and norms. And so just the expectation that our board aides are adhering to those policies as well because they are representing their respective board members.

Thank you. But to be clear, for my purposes, if an aide were to commit some transgression in violation of our policies or of their NDA, if that specific member did not agree with a potential recommendation to terminate the aide, is that the end of the conversation?

Is there any other recourse? So beginning on lines 219, it is, I'm going to get the exact letter and number for you if you give me a second, section E under number 4D. And it talks about while the board at large may not have oversight over individual board aides per policy 1035, board members could face disciplinary actions.

And it gives you some examples there for the acts of their respective board aides conduct. So that's where that's captured, it's captured there. Okay, and thank you. Going along with that, you mentioned the references to policies, I believe, 1030 and 1035.

I believe the language currently in this is that aides should, quote, be aware of those policies. In your mind, what is that conveying? Are aides subject to, required to follow these policies in as much as, obviously, some terms are only going to be applicable to members themselves?

Ms. Donahue, that is my understanding. I'd like to ask Division Council for any interpretation. they may have in terms of being aware, but it's my understanding that we'd say they need to be aware of it. It's also because they are representing their board members and what are the expectations for board members and so representing them in that capacity that they should be aware of the expectations of the board members and thus the aides.

But I'd like to ask for clarification from Division Council. - Thank you, Dr. Smith. Yes, I believe that's the intent and purpose of including that. - Thank you, Mr. Allen and Dr. Smith. So aides are not, as of right now, aides are not required to follow those policies, to adhere to those policies.

- Thank you, Ms. Donahue. Pursuant to the plain language, that's a reasonable interpretation, but if there's a lack of clarity or if the committee so chooses to provide clarity around that, it could so choose. - Okay, thank you, Mr. Allen. For consideration for my colleagues, I would support some changes, additional changes to this policy to make it more clear that the provisions policies 1030 and 1035 that could apply to board aides that the aids be required

and expected to follow those policies I do have two other questions if the chair will indulge me thank you so my first question is with regard to leave and I apologize that I did not flag specific line numbers here but I noted that there is one provision that states something about um i believe getting permission from the member if the aid is going to take leave and but then in the next provision states there is no personal leave

so can you can you please clarify how those provisions work together do you can you tell me which section you're referring to if you don't mind i i have one pulled up i just want to make sure i am i neglected to write down page numbers so i'm not sure either i'm line 120 and 124 Thank you, Ms. Catherine.

- Yes, and so, Ms. Donahue, in reference to this, the intent here is that board aides really serve in terms of hourly pay, and so they're only paid for which time that they work, and so they don't receive leave, and I wanna read this again in case there's, if there needs any clarity to make sure that is clear, but they are paid hourly for the work that they serve, and as you know, some weeks it might be 10 hours, some weeks it might be 40, anywhere in between, and so it's really only paid for the hours in which they work, and they do not have leave.

So if you feel like we need to be more clear in that policy and make changes, happy to do that. Thank you, Dr. Smith. I gather that was likely the intent here. I just was confused by those three words, and leave taken after hours worked. My last question is with regard to political activity.

There's a prohibition in here, which I do believe is appropriate, restricting board aides from engaging in political activity while they are on member time. I don't recall seeing a definition of political activity in this policy.
I realize we do define it in other policies, so I was wondering about that. So I think in terms of that, if we feel like there needs to be a separate definition here, we can do that.

We can also make a reference to where it is defined in other policies, if that would be helpful. But again, we want to make sure everybody's clear on this. We're happy to take your direction on that. If you'd like a separate definition or for us to pull it from another place or make a reference, we're happy to do that. I guess my biggest question with regard to that is I believe in other policies, LCPS defines political activity specifically as advocating for or against a specific political candidate, political party, a person running in an election or a matter that is before or subject to an election for a referendum or other matter.
And so in my mind, I am curious, would that extend to matters that may come before the board that are of public focus and disagreement that the board may have to decide on?

I guess, for example, if the board has a vote on policy 80-40 coming up, is it acceptable for board aides to be commenting on board time for or against that policy or any other policy that the board is facing a decision about?

My presumption is right now, if we go with the traditional definition of political activity, that it would not encompass such circumstances. So I guess that's my – the question that I am throwing out there is do my co-members think that it needs to be broader, if it is legally permitted to be broader, Mr. Allen?

Yes, I would start with that question. Under the way the policy is currently written, does it include perhaps even organizing activities or speakers? And if it – well, I guess we'll start with that. Thank you.

As I understand it, you know, board members are politically elected. This contemplates more so, as I understand it, kind of campaigning and those types of political activities. I mean, school board members are entitled to have political views and opinions and are elected on those.

Ms. Donahue, do you have any further questions? I do. Thank you. sure thank you um i understand that with the entire board now employing at least one or more aids i i do appreciate the need to kind of clarify the roles and the process related as i spoke about you know school board communication i think this was the next step too as this is not new new but

it is relatively new um and to really understand especially those boundaries between the board member and their aide, but also the board member and the staff, and kind of navigate all of that in terms of what is, you know, a perceivable request, how can we get the communication in terms of data in a timely manner, but we also want to ensure that the board is not inundating staff with data requests, and honestly, like, when I read this policy, I am a little concerned that we are crossing over into sort of a question of professionalism

And it talks about in policy 1035, section A3, it talks about board members, and it's about school board, maintaining awareness of different roles that school board members play, such as board members, citizen, parent. I mean, I'm on a PTA, but I'm also a school board member, and there are boundaries there.

And I understand why those boundaries exist, but I'm still allowed to be on my PTA. So I guess I have some, I take a little bit of concern and issue with mandating through policy that they cannot participate in local government when it affects them.

A lot of our aides are involved in school board happenings because they're here at every meeting with us. They obviously have an interest in the work that we do. So I would like to kind of flush that out a little bit more, especially as it pertains to Section B to Line J, or J, not Line J, but J, and ask that question, do we believe that being a board aide means you forsake your ability to participate in the local government and to use your First Amendment rights to participate if they personally disagree, even with you or with other board members?

I think it's a gray area, and I would appreciate especially your insight, Ms. Chandler, having walked the path. And I'll just add one more thing, because there's one more thing I want you to elaborate on, is in terms of the political nature is, you know, you did campaign while you were a staff aide.

And so how do we define those boundaries, not only just participating in meetings, but where do we draw those lines? because is coming to a board meeting, is that a campaign activity? If you then use that in your campaign materials to report out what the board talked about, that's public information, but you're also reporting to a staff aide.

So I'm not trying to make it too, too complicated, but I also think we could draw some lines that maybe we're not comfortable with if we set these things in policy. Thank you, Ms. Chernoff. It is a very interesting question, and I would really look forward to having a fuller discussion about it, perhaps as we move towards action.

I will say perhaps an easy line of delineation would be around whether or not you're getting paid while you're here, especially if you're participating in activism. And I would say that, I mean, are you going to speak?

I personally chose, I did participate in public comment quite a lot from 2017 until I was hired to serve as a staff aide. That feels like a good delineation to me. Of course, I would be happy to hear from staff if you have any other thoughts.

Yeah, thanks for that clarification, Ms. Chandler. I think that's how we've interpreted it as well. It's about when you're getting paid for the work, when you're receiving compensation, that you are on LCPS time and that, so you're completing LCPS activities and work.

And so that would not include the restricted and prohibited activities that shared in this policy. And so we would want to make sure that's clear, but that's how we've interpreted as well as when you are receiving payment for hours worked during that time.

- Mr. Allen, do you have anything to add? - Thank you, Madam Chair. That's my understanding as well. I would, in respect to letter J that Ms. Chernoff pointed out, it does say either publicly or privately.

And it's a decision for this committee and the board at large, whether they would like to retain the language or the spirit of the language that applies to school board members to refrain from conduct that may interfere with the school board's operations or decisions.

I think that that's up to you. You need to have that communication with your aid. we need to be very clear if that is not allowed or is, and what we're comfortable with. From my review of the NDA and this policy, there did seem to be discrepancies, and so we are trying to reconcile in policy, and then that's why there's a clarification that any time we do freshen up this policy, the school board freshens up this policy, then the NDA should, to the extent there's any material updates to this policy, be consistent with the NDA.

And in terms of the language regarding confidentiality the treatment of confidential information, they were currently at odds, and so that's why there's more specified language here to bring harmony to those discrepancies. Okay, I may need further clarification with you on that at a later time. I just want to make sure that I'm kind of still confused about the need to sign an NDA, but then to also have this basically says they can't have confidential information. That's kind of the way that I read it, so just feel like that's a little a little bit contradictory,

but maybe that's what you're saying. - Thank you, Ms. Chernoff. That's precisely what I was saying. The policy 2610 and its current iteration is at odds with the NDA, and so the current policy 2610 indicates that school board aides are not entitled to have confidential information at all currently, but that's subject to your decision making if you want to amend that bring it closer in line with what's currently in the NDAs. So happy to have you all consider that.

Yeah, I'd like those to be aligned. I think that that makes more sense. And then if we keep the clause in there about when the NDA is updated, that the policy follows the NDA, that would be my recommendation. That seems to make more sense. But again, we can continue to have those conversations. And overall, I just want to make sure that we're maintaining professional respect of aides and trusting them and trusting board members to make sure that they have that communication and oversight because they do report to us.

They don't report to staff. There are employees, not LCPS employees, as the policy states. So I don't know how we want to proceed, if we want to continue to have this as information and present our amendments at the next meeting or if we should do that in between. I would be open to what the chair would direct us on that.

Thank you, Ms. Chernoff. Ms. Donahue, do you have any more questions or comments? Thank you, Chair Chandler. I did want to follow up briefly. I appreciate Ms. Chernoff raising that issue because it's not something that had jumped out to me when I was reading the policy so much.

But to the extent that it's clear board aides are not permitted to have access to specific categories of information that a layperson might consider confidential, such as attorney-client communications or private personnel matters, I think that's very clear and agreed upon.

And the gray area would come into instances that don't fall into those categories, such as if my board aide knows how I'm going to vote on a particular matter that's coming before the school board or the committee, or someone else's board aide knows how I'm going to vote on a particular matter that's going to come before the committee or before the full board.

I would not feel comfortable ever with the possibility that that person might disclose that information without my knowledge or approval. So I agree with you that we need to make sure that we're being very clear in the language of the policy and the NDA about what information our aides are permitted to have access to and what we are expecting them, while they may have access to it, to not disclose beyond their conversations directly with their own members.

Thank you. Thank you, Ms. Donahue. I guess just as we wrap up this conversation, I would like to reflect back on some of the ways this policy has changed since it was created, I believe, in 2020. I do believe at some point in the past the school board had the right to approve whether or not a school board aide was hired.

I believe that the entire board had the ability to vote on the school board aides. Does anybody have any information about that? That was before my time. I can't speak to it. I'm sorry. I was worried about that.
